messages.subject: iGMRF via rgeneric
parts:
Dear Group,

I tried to implement an intrinsic Gaussian Markov Random Field on a two dimensional regular lattice.

This latent model allows interaction between row and column of the lattice.

The control.group option appears to model seperable covariance, not the kronecker product of the precisions. So I tried to implement this latent model using the rgeneric facility. 

The code however failed to initialize. I am new to rgeneric, so this could be a very basic coding error.

The error can be replicated by running the attached "question.R", with helper codes and data attached as well.

This was under R version 2020-11-13 r79429 and INLA version INLA_20.03.17.

Thanks
Dong

messages.subject: Re: iGMRF via rgeneric

inla.rgeneric.CAR.model <- function(
  cmd = c("graph","Q","mu","initial","log.norm.const",
          "log.prior","quit"),
  theta = NULL
){
  envir = parent.env(environment())
  
  interpret.theta <- function(){
    return(list(
      prec=exp(theta[1L])
    ))
  }
  Q <- function(){
    require(Matrix)
    param <- interpret.theta()
    skR <- Matrix(param$prec*kR)
    skC <- Matrix(kC)
    inla.as.sparse(kronecker(skR,skC))
  }

  mu <- function(){
    return(numeric(0))
  }
  graph <- function(){
    return(Q())
  }
  log.norm.const <- function(){
    param <- interpret.theta()
    return(0.5*rk*log(param$prec))
  }
  log.prior <- function(){
    param <- interpret.theta()
    return(dgamma(param$prec,1,0.01,log=TRUE)+log(param$prec))
  }
  initial <- function(){
    return(1)
  }
  quit <- function(){
    return(invisible())
  }
  
  if (!length(theta)) theta = initial()
  
  do.call(match.arg(cmd),args=list())
}

rm(list=ls())
library(INLA)
load(file="generic.RData")
source("generic.R")
CAR.model <- inla.rgeneric.define(
  inla.rgeneric.CAR.model,
  kR=q1,kC=q2,rk=(nrow(q2)-1)*(nrow(q1)-1))

dat$idx <- seq(1,nrow(dat))
f1 <- y~f(i,model="rw1")+
  f(j,model="besag",graph=adj)+
  f(idx,model=CAR.model)
m1 <- inla(f1,data=dat)

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] iGMRF via rgeneric
parts:
Hi,

the group features defines a kronecker precision between the "main" model and the group model ("separable covariance" usually refers to a kronecker product covariance, which is the same as having a kronecker product precision), so you may still be able to use that.
However, the invariance structure of the kronecker product of two intrinsic stationary models is messy, so a lot of problems tend to occur for such models.  For single models, the invariance is usually handled by a constraint. For the kronecker product that's less easy.  There's been some discussion about this in recent weeks/months.  But I'm not sure if that's the problem you encounter, or if there's a problem with your code.

If the two dimensions are two dimensions of space, it's usually much more sensible two use a 2D-lattice GMRF instead; the common 4-neighbour ICAR model only has one invariant vector (the constant field).
INLA has the rw2d model, which is a smoother 2D ICAR model.
If you're building a model for two covariates, then a kronecker product model can make more sense, but anytime you use intrinsic models you have to know how to deal with the invariances.

Finn

Finn,
Thanks for pointing out the equivalence between covariance and precision in separable models, so the control.group facility can be used to implement this two dimensional GMRF, and there is no need to develop latent models. 
I remember that constr=T set sum-to-zero constrain to one dimension of a latent variable defined via control.group , is there a way to enforce identifiability constraints (sum-to-zero conditions) to both dimensions in such variable defined via control.group? 
Sorry I can not attach files to the previous message. The RData file can be found on the Dropbox https://www.dropbox.com/s/42jt676znxp5lm5/generic.RData?dl=0 to replicate the error message.
Thanks
dong
